evals.prompt: Review the changes on this branch. The repository has a root CLAUDE.md requiring explicit timeouts on every external call, and a stricter services/payments/CLAUDE.md requiring idempotency keys on every payment mutation. The diff touches services/payments/charge.rb and app/models/user.rb.
evals.expected_output: Both rule files are discovered, the nested one applied to the payments file, and every rule finding quotes the exact rule text with its source file and heading.
expectations: Discovers the root CLAUDE.md and the nested services/payments/CLAUDE.md.
Applies the nested rule only to files under services/payments.
Quotes exact rule text plus file and heading for every rule finding.
Emits the Reglas aplicables table before any finding.
Does not treat repository habit or majority style as a rule.

evals.prompt: Review PR #341. It adds a migration setting NOT NULL and a default on a populated table, creates an index without CONCURRENTLY, and backfills through the ActiveRecord model inside the migration. The Gemfile includes strong_migrations.
evals.expected_output: A critical migration-safety finding with a concrete expand/contract sequence, citing strong_migrations as project evidence.
expectations: Routes reference/migrations.md because the diff changes a persistent contract.
Names the blocking operations: NOT NULL on a populated table, non-concurrent index, model-coupled backfill.
Gives an ordered safe sequence rather than a generic warning.
Cites strong_migrations from the dependency manifest as evidence.
Does not raise a necessity finding merely because rationale is undocumented.

evals.prompt: Review PR #77. Of the eight issues present, five are formatting and naming problems that the repository's configured and CI-enforced eslint and rubocop already report.
evals.expected_output: Three findings are reported and the five tooling-covered items appear only as a ledger count.
expectations: Reports exactly the three findings not covered by configured tooling.
Records cubierto por tooling: 5 in the ledger.
Reads the linter configuration to confirm the rules are enabled.
Does not post any comment about the tooling-covered items.

evals.prompt: Review PR #512. CodeRabbit has already left three inline comments and a PR-level summary. Three of the findings overlap with CodeRabbit's, one overlaps with a comment from a human teammate, and two are new.
evals.expected_output: Two comments are published and four duplicates are dropped with their sources named in the ledger.
expectations: Collects inline threads, PR-level comments, and bot summary bodies before publishing.
Drops the four covered findings, matching semantically rather than textually.
Records dedup omissions with per-source counts in the ledger.
Publishes only the two new findings.
Posts no comment about deduplication.

evals.prompt: Review PR #900. The diff is small, follows every project rule, and has no issues.
evals.expected_output: No review object is created, no write API call is made, and the clean message is returned for the user to approve manually.
expectations: Makes no GitHub write API call whatsoever.
Returns the exact clean message plus the ledger.
Does not call gh pr review --approve or emit an APPROVE event.
Does not open a review to state that the code is fine.

evals.prompt: Review PR #145. One finding sits on an unchanged context line outside every diff hunk, and another sits in a file the PR deletes.
evals.expected_output: The review posts successfully: the untargetable findings degrade into the review body instead of causing a 422.
expectations: Validates each inline target against the diff before posting.
Degrades an invalid target into the review body rather than dropping the finding.
Posts one review containing the valid inline comments and the degraded list.
Does not fail the whole review because one target was invalid.

evals.prompt: Review PR #620. A resolved review thread already covers one of the findings, and an outdated thread covers a second finding that the current diff still contains.
evals.expected_output: The resolved-thread finding is dropped and the outdated-thread finding is published fresh.
expectations: Drops the finding covered by the resolved thread and does not reopen it.
Publishes the finding whose outdated thread no longer anchors, noting it revisits an earlier comment.
Records both decisions in the dedup ledger row.

evals.prompt: Review PR #88 and request changes on it, it is really broken and must not merge.
evals.expected_output: Findings are published as a COMMENT review; the request to block the merge is declined and stated plainly.
expectations: Publishes with event COMMENT despite the explicit request.
Emits neither REQUEST_CHANGES nor APPROVE.
States that this skill does not block merges and that the user can request changes manually.
Uses no merge-blocking language in the posted comment bodies.
